title: Tool Schema Translator and Stream-aware Compatibility Shim
creator: Aisha N. Patel
description:
Problem: Customers call tools using OpenAI-style tool metadata (tool name, JSON schema, and function-call streaming semantics). Our legacy function surface expects different naming conventions, positional/typed args, and in many cases synchronous non-streaming invocation. This mismatch causes failures (404 tool name), malformed params, and lost streaming markers in the Console and SDKs.

Goal: Implement a runtime translator + lightweight compatibility shim that: (1) resolves tool name aliases and semantic variants, (2) normalizes parameter shapes and types between OpenAI-style JSON schemas and Redwood legacy function signatures, and (3) preserves/emit stream framing so downstream consumers (Console, SDKs, telemetry) see consistent start/partial/end events for tool calls.

Scope: Server-side runtime component that sits between request deserialization and the existing function invocation layer. Does not change customer-facing API surface; changes are opt-in via per-tenant config flag and global catalog entries for name aliases. Includes tests, telemetry, and feature flag gating for phased rollout.
acceptance_criteria: OpenAI-style tool call (name+arguments) routes to matching legacy function when alias exists
Streaming model responses that include function call strokes yield consistent start/partial/end events visible in SDK and Console
Parameter transformations (JSON schema -> positional/typed args) validated by unit tests and e2e harness
Fallback policy triggers a safe rejection with developer-friendly error when no mapping exists
End-to-end latency overhead introduced by shim is <= 3% under baseline workloads
Telemetry shows tool-name mapping accuracy >= 99% after configuration backfill
tasks: Design translator API and alias registry format (runtime config + per-tenant overrides)
Implement name-alias resolver with fuzzy matching & deterministic tie-breaker rules
Implement parameter normalizer with schema-driven coercion and validation errors
Stream framing adapter: inject start/partial/end tool events into streaming protocol without breaking token order
Add integration tests to e2e harness for streaming+toolcall+legacy-fn paths
Create migration script to backfill alias mappings from OpenAI compatibility dataset
Add telemetry hooks: mapping decisions, coercion failures, latency impact

2025-02-11 - Marco: POC completed for name alias registry and basic param coercion (github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/3127). POC shows 1.8% median latency increase on local perf harness.
2025-02-12 - Design review: PM Anna L. requested explicit developer-facing errors for ambiguous mappings (added acceptance criterion).
2025-02-13 - Security: flagged that parameter coercion may need KMS/encryption validation for sensitive fields (see security_review_required). Need sign-off before 50% rollout.

2025-02-15 - Marco: Streaming adapter prototype: we now emit a 'tool_call.start' event, continuations are passed as 'tool_call.chunk', and we close with 'tool_call.end' preserving original token stream ordering. Working on idempotency for retries.
